summary: Decision 8 pass (batch rs-cbi-7): rules each document states that were already recorded from other sources, now recorded from this document too.

program_terms.applies_to: each investor: full-time positions for qualifying employees created by the new commercial enterprise
program_terms.location: p. 4, Background (A. The EB-5 Program), line 21
program_terms.quote: when they invest money in American businesses that create at least ten American jobs.
program_terms.notes: Restates the statute (8 U.S.C. 1153(b)(5)) as described by the court. Number written in words. Validity dates not stated.

program_terms.applies_to: investor (spouse and children under 21 included); standard amount outside targeted employment areas
program_terms.quote: Until 2017, Homeland Security maintained the standard EB-5 investment threshold at $1 million and the reduced investment threshold at $500,000, as originally set by the INA in 1990.
program_terms.notes: Restates the 1990 statute. The court gives 1990 as the start; the amount applied until the 2019 rule took effect, which the order says happened on 21 November 2019 (p. 5, lines 23-24), so valid_to is the day before. p. 4 also: 'the amount of capital required to obtain such a visa is $1,000,000'.

program_terms.applies_to: investor; targeted employment area (rural or at least 150% of national unemployment)
program_terms.quote: Until 2017, Homeland Security maintained the standard EB-5 investment threshold at $1 million and the reduced investment threshold at $500,000, as originally set by the INA in 1990.
program_terms.notes: Restates the 1990 statute. p. 4 also: 'If investors make investments in targeted employment areas, the threshold amount of capital required is lowered to $500,000.' Dates as for the standard amount: 1990 per the court, until the 2019 rule took effect on 21 November 2019.

program_terms.applies_to: investor; standard amount (also applied in high-employment areas)
program_terms.quote: increased the standard investment threshold to $1.8 million and the reduced investment threshold to $900,000.
program_terms.notes: Restates the 2019 Modernization rule; the order says it went into effect on 21 November 2019. This order (22 June 2021) vacates the rule; valid_to left empty because the order does not state an end date for the amount as such.

program_terms.applies_to: investor; targeted employment area
program_terms.quote: increased the standard investment threshold to $1.8 million and the reduced investment threshold to $900,000.
program_terms.notes: Restates the 2019 Modernization rule; in effect from 21 November 2019 per the order, which vacates the rule. valid_to left empty (not stated as a date for the amount).

program_terms.applies_to: investor (spouse and children under 21 included); standard amount outside targeted employment areas
program_terms.quote: The EB-5 program requires that the foreign investor make a capital investment of either $500,000 or $1 million, depending on whether or not the investment is in a high-unemployment area.
program_terms.notes: Restates the statute and regulations as described by DHS OIG (December 2013). Validity dates not stated.

program_terms.applies_to: investor; targeted employment area (rural or at least 150% of national unemployment)
program_terms.quote: The EB-5 program requires that the foreign investor make a capital investment of either $500,000 or $1 million, depending on whether or not the investment is in a high-unemployment area.
program_terms.notes: Restates the statute and regulations. The report speaks of high-unemployment areas only (p. 10: 'qualifies for the lower foreign investment of $500,000'); applies_to kept as on the existing targeted-employment-area rows so the restatement links. Validity dates not stated.

program_terms.applies_to: each investor: full-time positions for qualifying employees created by the new commercial enterprise
program_terms.quote: which will create or preserve at least 10 full-time jobs, for qualifying U.S. workers, within 2 years of receiving conditional permanent residency.
program_terms.notes: Restates the statute and regulations. The report includes preserved jobs and a 2-year window. Validity dates not stated.

program_terms.applies_to: investor and derivative family members: conditional permanent residence before removal of conditions
program_terms.quote: If the Form I-526 petition is approved, the investor obtains conditional permanent residency and has 2 years to fulfill the program requirements of job creation and capital investment.
program_terms.notes: Restates INA 216A as described by DHS OIG. Validity dates not stated.

program_terms.applies_to: investor (spouse and children under 21 included); standard amount outside targeted employment areas
program_terms.location: PDF p. 11, Background; also PDF p. 19, footnote 8
program_terms.quote: The EB-5 program requires that the foreign investor make a capital investment of either $500,000 or $1 million, depending on whether or not the investment is in a high-unemployment area, known as a Targeted Employment Area.
program_terms.notes: Restates the statute and regulations as described by DHS OIG (March 2015). Footnote 8: 'an investor only has to invest $500,000 (rather than $1,000,000 in other areas)'. Validity dates not stated.

program_terms.applies_to: investor; targeted employment area (rural or at least 150% of national unemployment)
program_terms.location: PDF p. 11, Background; also PDF p. 19, footnote 8
program_terms.quote: By investing in a Targeted Employment Area an investor only has to invest $500,000 (rather than $1,000,000 in other areas) to be eligible for temporary residence status.
program_terms.notes: Restates the statute and regulations. The report does not define a targeted employment area beyond 'high-unemployment area'; applies_to kept as on the existing rows so the restatement links. Validity dates not stated.

program_terms.applies_to: each investor: full-time positions for qualifying employees created by the new commercial enterprise
program_terms.quote: which will create or preserve at least 10 full-time jobs for qualifying U.S. workers, within two years of receiving conditional permanent residency.
program_terms.notes: Restates the statute and regulations; the report includes preserved jobs and a two-year window. Validity dates not stated.

program_terms.applies_to: investor and derivative family members: conditional permanent residence before removal of conditions
program_terms.quote: If the Form I-526 petition is approved, the investor obtains conditional permanent residency and has two years to fulfill the program requirements of job creation and capital investment.
program_terms.notes: Restates INA 216A as described by DHS OIG. Number written in words. Validity dates not stated.

program_terms.applies_to: investor; minimum as stated by the source (no distinction between targeted employment areas and other areas)
program_terms.quote: which provides lawful permanent residence – commonly known as a “Green Card” – to foreign nationals who invest at least $500,000 in a domestic business that creates 10 new American jobs.
program_terms.notes: DOJ press release (27 Nov 2017) gives USD 500,000 as the EB-5 minimum without saying it applied only in targeted employment areas (USD 1,000,000 elsewhere under the statute). Kept as stated, under its own applies_to so it is not linked to the targeted-employment-area rows. Validity dates not stated.

program_terms.applies_to: each investor: full-time positions for qualifying employees created by the new commercial enterprise
program_terms.quote: nor did it lead to the creation of 10 new American full-time jobs, as required under the program.
program_terms.notes: Restates the statute as described by DOJ. Validity dates not stated.

program_terms.applies_to: investor (spouse and children under 21 included); standard amount outside targeted employment areas
program_terms.quote: The visa program permits immigrants to invest a minimum of $1,000,000.00 in a United States job-creating enterprise and obtain permanent residency if, after two years, that investment created or preserved ten American jobs.
program_terms.notes: Restates the statute as described by DOJ (22 June 2021), in the past tense. Validity dates not stated.

program_terms.applies_to: investor; targeted employment area (rural or at least 150% of national unemployment)
program_terms.quote: The minimum investment required was lowered to $500,000.00 if the investment was made in a targeted employment area (“TEA”), defined as an area with an unemployment rate of 150% of the national average.
program_terms.notes: Restates the statute as described by DOJ. The release mentions only the unemployment criterion, not rural areas; applies_to kept as on the existing rows so the restatement links. Validity dates not stated.

program_terms.applies_to: each investor: full-time positions for qualifying employees created by the new commercial enterprise
program_terms.quote: obtain permanent residency if, after two years, that investment created or preserved ten American jobs.
program_terms.notes: Restates the statute as described by DOJ; number written in words; includes preserved jobs. Validity dates not stated.

program_terms.applies_to: investor (spouse and children under 21 included); standard amount outside targeted employment areas
program_terms.quote: make an investment of a minimum of $1 million, or $500,000 if the investment is made in certain areas of high unemployment.
program_terms.notes: Restates the statute as described by DOJ (22 July 2021). Validity dates not stated.

program_terms.applies_to: investor; targeted employment area (rural or at least 150% of national unemployment)
program_terms.quote: make an investment of a minimum of $1 million, or $500,000 if the investment is made in certain areas of high unemployment.
program_terms.notes: Restates the statute as described by DOJ, which mentions only areas of high unemployment; applies_to kept as on the existing rows so the restatement links. Validity dates not stated.

program_terms.applies_to: investor and derivative family members: conditional permanent residence before removal of conditions
program_terms.quote: To receive a two-year grant of conditional permanent residency status, foreign investors must meet certain requirements for an entry visa
program_terms.notes: Restates INA 216A as described by DOJ. Number written in words. Validity dates not stated.

program_terms.applies_to: each investor: full-time positions for qualifying employees created by the new commercial enterprise
program_terms.quote: including the creation of at least 10 jobs for United States citizens and residents through the business funded by the investment.
program_terms.notes: Restates the statute as described by DOJ. Validity dates not stated.

program_terms.notes: Administrative rule; the change itself is already an event from this source. No existing row for this rule from another source. valid_from is the month the page gives; end not stated.

ledger.contains: Order of the US District Court, N.D. Cal. (22 June 2021, 17 pages) in Behring Regional Center LLC v. Wolf granting summary judgment: background on the EB-5 programme and the 2019 Modernization Rule, analysis under the Federal Vacancies Reform Act, and vacatur of the rule (already an event). Programme numbers: the annual allocation of 9,940 EB-5 visas with at least 3,000 reserved for targeted employment areas (now extracted as planned places, status budget). Rules restated from statute and the 2019 rule ($1,000,000 standard / $500,000 TEA minimum; $1.8 million / $900,000 under the 2019 rule; TEA = rural area or unemployment of at least 150% of the national average; rural = outside a metropolitan area or town of 20,000 or more) are already in program_terms from the statute and Federal Register. Other numbers are dates and legal citations. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Order of the US District Court, N.D. Cal. (24 June 2022, 14 pages) in Behring Regional Center LLC v. Mayorkas granting a preliminary injunction: USCIS may not treat regional centers designated before the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022 as deauthorized (already an event). Programme numbers: more than 600 regional centers operating as of 2021 / '600-plus' when the Act took effect (now extracted once, as of 2021). The six-month non-binding target for deciding new I-956 applications is extracted as a processing-time target (status budget). Rules and dates restated (pilot programme of 1992 with a 1997 sunset, lapse June 2021, Act effective 15 March 2022, authorisation to September 2027) are already in the programme notes and events. Out of scope: 'over 100 regional centers' represented by an amicus seeking to intervene (case-level), case-management dates. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

DHS OIG audit report OIG-14-19 (12 Dec 2013, 40 pages) on the EB-5 Regional Center Program: findings, four recommendations, Appendix A (scope), Appendix B (USCIS management comments of 4 Nov 2013, a scan with an imperfect text layer), contributors, distribution. Programme numbers: 325 approved regional centers at 1 Oct 2013 (already in the data); USCIS's unsupported cumulative figures since 1990 (more than $6.8 billion invested, at least 49,000 jobs); FY2012 regional center applications approved (35) and denied (63); 336 regional centers with I-924 filings in FY2010-FY2012; regional-center fees of $25,000-$50,000 per investor - all now extracted. Rule and timeline items added as events: 'pilot' dropped 3 Aug 2012, Form I-924 required from 2010, annual I-924A from 2011, policy memorandum 30 May 2013 (the report's own release is already an event). The opening of the Immigrant Investor Program Office (May 2013, Appendix B) is recorded as an event from usa-dhsoig-eb5-mayorkas-2015, which gives the exact day. The $500,000 / $1 million minimum investment is restated as background and is already in program_terms from the statute and regulations. Out of scope: single-case audit findings (12 of 15 files reviewed, a project 82% funded by US investors, a hotel costing about $28 million with $4.5 million of foreign money), audit sample sizes (15 regional center files, 6 investor files, 22 cases), and USCIS staffing (9 EB-5 staff in 2009, more than 80 in 2013, 7 then 9 economists, 22 economists). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

DHS OIG investigation report (24 Mar 2015, 99 pages) into employee complaints about Director Mayorkas's handling of EB-5 matters: summary, background on the programme and petition process, three case narratives (LA Films, Las Vegas/SLS, Gulf Coast), timelines (Appendices A-B) and Mr. Mayorkas's 32-page statement (Appendix C, a scan). Programme numbers, all now extracted: about 641 regional centers approved at 2 Mar 2015; FY2012 I-526 petitions filed (6,041) and approved (3,677) and I-829 approvals (736) - all three match the USCIS data already in the dataset; USCIS wait times at January 2015 (I-526 14.2, I-829 12.3, I-924 11.7 months); more than 700 regional center applications 'in the three years in question' (years not stated); regional-center fees of $25,000-$50,000 per investor; and, as a rule, the $6,230 regional center application fee charged from the 2010 fee rule (Appendix C). Event added: Immigrant Investor Program Office opened 6 May 2013 (the report itself is already an event). The $500,000 / $1 million minimum and the 10-job requirement are restated background, already in program_terms from primary sources. Out of scope: case-level figures (more than 200 LA Films III petitions, 240/249 LA Films IV petitions, about 230 SLS investors of whom 47 had filed by 23 Jan 2013, Gulf Coast $555,000 units), investigation statistics (about 50 interviews, more than 40,000 call records, more than 15 witnesses), and USCIS-wide figures (about 19,000 staff, 223 offices, 6,100 green cards and 3,200 naturalisations a day, 2007 fee rise of about 86%). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

DOJ (US Attorney, C.D. Cal.) press release of 27 Nov 2017: attorney Victoria Chan pleads guilty in the California Investment Immigration Fund EB-5 scheme (already an event). Figures: more than $50 million collected from more than 100 mainly Chinese investors, about 130 fraudulent EB-5 applications, eight properties worth nearly $25 million to be forfeited, homes worth nearly $1 million each bought with 'hundreds of thousands of dollars' of investor funds, 45-year statutory maximum. Case-level figures describe the case and are in the existing event's description where relevant; they are not programme statistics and match no indicator (no amount of investor money misused is stated). Programme rules restated in the release (minimum investment of $500,000, 10 new jobs) are already in program_terms from primary sources. Related-content links at the foot of the page are unrelated. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

DOJ (US Attorney, E.D. La.) press release of 22 June 2021: operators of the New Orleans EB-5 Regional Center sentenced to 102 months each (already an event). Figures: 31 immigrants invested $15.5 million ($500,000 each in a targeted employment area) plus service fees; $18,070,000 obtained from all investors including one non-immigrant; funds 'fraudulently misappropriated' but no amount stated; restitution left for later. Case-level figures describe the case and are in the existing event's description where relevant; they are not programme statistics and match no indicator (no amount of investor money misused is stated). Programme rules restated in the release (minimum investment $1,000,000 / $500,000 in targeted employment areas, 10 jobs, two-year conditional residence) are already in program_terms from primary sources. Related-content links at the foot of the page are unrelated. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

DOJ (US Attorney, N.D. Cal.) press release of 22 July 2021: Thomas Henderson (San Francisco Regional Center) and Cooper Lee plead guilty (already an event). Figures: SFRC raised more than $100 million from foreign investors for seven EB-5 enterprises in 2011-2017; funds from 42 investors in North America 3PL LP used for other projects (amount not stated); statutory maximum penalties. Case-level figures describe the case and are in the existing event's description where relevant; they are not programme statistics and match no indicator (no amount of investor money misused is stated). Programme rules restated in the release (minimum investment $1,000,000 / $500,000 in targeted employment areas, 10 jobs, two-year conditional residence) are already in program_terms from primary sources. Related-content links at the foot of the page are unrelated. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

USCIS web page (updated 13 May 2026): number of approved regional centers ("As of May 11, 2026, there are 567 approved regional centers", already in the data), alert that the 2022 law authorises the Regional Center Program through 30 Sept 2027 (already in events from other sources), contact details, disclaimers, note that earlier I-526/I-829 statistics by regional center are under review. The table of regional centers by state is loaded by script and its body is empty in the stored copy (only the headers State / Regional Center / Regional Center ID); it holds names, not numbers, and counting rows would be a calculation. Nothing new added. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

USCIS web page (updated 18 Nov 2025) on EB-5 requirements: alert on the 14 Nov 2025 Form G-1055 fee schedule restoring pre-April 2024 fees (event added); programme history (1990 creation, 1992 regional center pilot, 15 Mar 2022 Reform and Integrity Act, regional center visas through 30 Sept 2027: already in events from other sources); new commercial enterprise definition (40% expansion test); job creation (10 jobs, 90% indirect for regional centers: added as terms); troubled business (2 years, 20% loss) and full-time (35 hours) definitions; capital definition; minimum investment table (before 15 Mar 2022 USD 1,000,000 / 500,000 / 1,000,000 high-employment; from 15 Mar 2022 USD 1,050,000 / 800,000: pre-2022 standard and TEA terms already in the data, the other three added); five-yearly CPI-U adjustment from 1 Jan 2027 (already in events); TEA definitions (150% unemployment, 20,000 population); visa set-asides 20% rural, 10% high unemployment, 2% infrastructure (added as terms). Not recorded as separate terms: definitional thresholds (40%, 2 years and 20% loss, 35 hours, 150%, 20,000), which define eligibility rather than set a price or quota. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

USCIS 'EB-5 What's New' page (updated 18 Nov 2025), a list of alerts: 14 Nov 2025 G-1055 fee schedule restoring pre-April 2024 fees (event recorded once, from usa-uscis-web-eb5-classification-2025); FY2025 Integrity Fund payments due 1 Oct 2024 and final deadline 30 Dec 2024 for FY2023-2025 with termination of non-payers (event added); regional center audits at least every five years (term added) and use of the Yellow Book standards 'Starting April 23' (year not printed: not recorded as an event); I-956G annual statements due 29 Dec 2023 (routine filing reminder, not recorded); Green Card validity extended 48 months for pending I-829s, Jan 2023 (event added); Behring settlement I-956 amendment deadline of 29 Dec 2022 lifted (event added); Integrity Fund USD 20,000 / 10,000 (term added); separate fee payments from 1 Sept 2022 (event added); Behring v. Mayorkas injunction 24 Jun 2022 (already in events); resumed processing of pre-June 2021 regional-center I-526s (undated: not recorded); notice to I-829 filers under Pub. L. 107-273 (I-829 filed before 2 Nov 2002 on I-526s approved 1 Jan 1995-31 Aug 1998; eligibility criteria, not recorded); 15 Mar 2022 law and program through 30 Sept 2027 (already in events); news item of 24 Jul 2020 on capital deployment guidance (event added). No statistics. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

USCIS form page for Form I-140G (updated 10 Dec 2025): form edition 11/19/25; online-only filing after registration on trumpcard.gov; fee USD 15,000 per person (principal, spouse, children). The fee (program_terms) and the form's publication (event) were already in the data; nothing else in scope. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Undated 3-page Citizenship Office fee schedule. Programme content: CIIP (Form D) citizenship fee USD 260,000 for main applicant, spouse and one child under 18 (already recorded), plus USD 19,250 per extra child under 18 or USD 44,250 per dependant aged 18-21 (now recorded); application fee VT5,000 for a first application 'applies to all application Forms' (recorded for CIIP with a warning: it conflicts with the USD 250 Form D fee elsewhere). Out of scope: ordinary naturalisation, marriage, entitlement and regain fees (Forms A-C), certificate replacement and search fees. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Citizenship Office directive of 30 April 2020 to DSP and VCP agents restating the prescribed government minimum contribution and minimum selling price for four family categories under Regulation Orders 33 and 34 of 2019, warning that agents underselling risk licence cancellation and applicants risk revocation. All 16 prices now recorded (DSP and VCP); event already recorded. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Citizenship Commission press release, 2 Dec 2024: reaction to EU visa decision, enhanced FIU/Interpol/Immigration due diligence, CIIP mandatory USD 50,000 investment component, biometric passports (capture systems abroad by March 2025, not programme-specific), agent agreements to lapse by January 2025. USD 50,000 term and reform event already recorded; nothing else in scope. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Citizenship Office 'Fees and Charges' web page (as of 2026-10-02). Programme content: table 'Government Mandated Fees' (programme not named; equals the DSP/VCP minimum selling prices): FIU diligence fee USD 5,000; single applicant USD 130,000 (already recorded); married couple 150,000; couple + 1 child 165,000; couple + 2 children 180,000; additional applicant 10,000 (now recorded under vut-dsp like the existing row); Form D (CIIP) application fee USD 250, citizenship fee USD 260,000 (already recorded), extra child USD 19,250, dependant 18-21 USD 44,250 (now recorded). Not recorded: the general VT5,000 application fee for Forms other than D (ordinary naturalisation forms, not a programme). Links to the 2013 and 2014 fee orders, stored separately. DSP (Amendment) Regulations Order No. 39 of 2020 (27 Mar 2020): agent quota of at least 12 investors a year, due diligence by an international specialist firm plus the FIU, FIU time limit changed from 48 to 96 hours (procedural, not tabled), due diligence fee USD2,000 to USD5,000. Fee change and event already recorded; agent quota taken. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

IMF 2024 Article IV staff report (CR 24/278, 94 pages).
